base_and_rev1_status: BOTH SEALED AND UNMODIFIED. This addendum rewrites neither. All three documents are pinned by the GO and re-hashed at preflight. Precedence is rev2 > rev1 > base.
scope: This addendum touches ONE thing: the normalisation rules of rev1. Every gate, every threshold, every protocol clause and every prohibition of the base document and of rev1 stands unchanged.

the_contradiction_being_resolved.rule_A: 'tensor_like_with_ndim_0_and_numeric_scalars': ('scalar', the exact Python value). A zero-dimensional float32 tensor holding 81.0 and a Python float 81.0 both normalise to ('scalar', 81.0).
the_contradiction_being_resolved.why_they_conflict: Adam's step is a Python float 81.0 in the checkpoint pickle and a zero-dimensional float32 tensor in the live optimizer. Rule A says both become ('scalar', 81.0). Rule B says the Python float becomes ('prim', 'float', 81.0). A reader implementing rule B before rule A produces a mismatch on all six step entries that is purely representational and has nothing to do with whether the restore worked.
the_contradiction_being_resolved.measured_evidence: with rule B applied first the comparison reports exactly six differences, all of the form optimizer.state.<i>.step, on a restore that is otherwise byte-identical. With rule A applied to Python numerics the comparison reports zero differences, and a single perturbed element of one moment tensor still reports exactly one difference. The check therefore loses no power.
the_contradiction_being_resolved.resolution: rule A governs. Rule B is narrowed to str and None.

normalisation_rules_as_they_now_stand.order_is_significant: the branches are evaluated in this order and the order is part of the specification
normalisation_rules_as_they_now_stand.1_bool: ('prim', 'bool', value). Evaluated FIRST, because bool is a subclass of int in Python and would otherwise be swallowed by the numeric branch.
normalisation_rules_as_they_now_stand.4_numeric_scalars: ('scalar', value) for Python int and float, for NumPy scalars, and for any zero-dimensional NumPy array or torch tensor. This is the branch that makes the checkpoint's Python float step and the live optimizer's 0-D tensor step compare equal, which is the entire reason this addendum exists.
normalisation_rules_as_they_now_stand.5_tensor_like_with_ndim_ge_1: ('tensor', dtype string with any 'torch.' prefix stripped, shape tuple, sha256 of the C-order bytes). This is where byte identity of exp_avg and exp_avg_sq is enforced and it is untouched by this addendum.
normalisation_rules_as_they_now_stand.6_list_and_tuple: ('seq', [normalised items]) - a tuple and a list with the same contents normalise equal, because betas survives the round trip as either
normalisation_rules_as_they_now_stand.7_dict: ('map', sorted list of (normalised key, normalised value)) - integer keys stay integers
normalisation_rules_as_they_now_stand.8_anything_else: ('opaque', type name), which can never equal a real value on the other side, so an unrecognised type fails closed

implementation_trap_recorded.what: numpy.ascontiguousarray promotes a zero-dimensional array to shape (1,).
implementation_trap_recorded.consequence_if_missed: reading ndim AFTER ascontiguousarray means the zero-dimensional branch is never reached, every scalar is hashed as a one-element tensor, and rule 4 silently does not apply.
implementation_trap_recorded.requirement: ndim MUST be read from the array before ascontiguousarray is called. This was observed in implementation, not theorised.

type_preservation_in_param_groups.concern: rule 4 compares numerics by value, so it does not distinguish an int 0 from a float 0.0.
type_preservation_in_param_groups.why_this_is_acceptable_here: the param_groups keys whose TYPE carries meaning are the five booleans - amsgrad, capturable, decoupled_weight_decay, differentiable, maximize - and the two None-valued keys foreach and fused. Rules 1 and 2 keep every one of those in typed prim form, so a bool that turned into a number, or a None that turned into a value, is still caught. The remaining keys - lr, eps, weight_decay, betas and the params index list - are numeric and are compared by exact value with ==, which is the invariant that matters for them.
what_is_therefore_still_detected: any change to lr, eps, weight_decay or betas
any change to the params index list, including its length or order
any of the five booleans flipping
foreach or fused ceasing to be None
any key appearing or disappearing on either side

tests_this_addendum_requires.T_step_representation: normalise(81.0) must equal normalise(torch.tensor(81.0)), and both must equal normalise(numpy.float32(81.0)). This is the exact source-versus-live case and it must be asserted explicitly rather than inferred from an end-to-end run.
tests_this_addendum_requires.T_bool_is_not_a_number: normalise(False) must NOT equal normalise(0), and normalise(True) must NOT equal normalise(1)
tests_this_addendum_requires.T_moment_corruption: perturbing a single element of exp_avg or exp_avg_sq must produce exactly one difference, naming that index and that key
tests_this_addendum_requires.T_param_groups_corruption: changing lr, changing weight_decay, flipping one boolean, dropping a key, and shortening the params list must each be detected
tests_this_addendum_requires.T_state_index_corruption: removing one of the six Adam entries, or adding a seventh, must be detected
tests_this_addendum_requires.T_ndim_zero_not_promoted: normalise of a 0-D tensor must yield a scalar, not a ('tensor', ..., (1,), ...) triple - the regression test for the ascontiguousarray trap
